figure: Figure A.3 (Chronology of frontier AI systems)
issue: The legend assigns semantic meaning to bar shade — 'Model architecture (dashed) — foundation, efficiency, MoE; darker shade = MoE ~2022' — but the three architecture bars use three distinct orange shades (Transformer light, Efficient Transformer medium, MoE dark) and only the darkest is explained. Inviting the reader to read shade as data while leaving two of three shades unexplained creates a small open question ('what do the lighter shades encode?') that the in-bar labels only implicitly answer.
evidence: Legend line (verbatim): 'Model architecture (dashed) — foundation, efficiency, MoE; darker shade = MoE ~2022'. Bars (verbatim labels): 'Transformer ~2017' (lightest orange), 'Efficient Transformer ~2020' (medium orange), 'MoE Transformer ~2022' (darkest orange). No other legend line references shade.
acceptance_test: Either extend the legend to state what the shade progression encodes (e.g., 'shade = era within the architecture family') or remove shade as a semantic channel (single orange for all three dashed bars), keeping the dashed/solid/thick border channels; re-render and confirm no legend line assigns meaning to an unexplained visual variable.

issue: The vertical stack of touching bars visually implies a cumulative stack, substrate, or causal lineage, directly contradicting the caption's disclaimer.
evidence: The figure arranges all stages as a single vertical column of bars with no gaps, each directly above the next. The caption explicitly says 'not a causal lineage and not a substrate stack' and instructs the reader to read it as 'what exists at each stage,' not 'what caused what.'
acceptance_test: Redesign as a timeline with separated markers or add visible gaps/arrows and an in-figure 'not cumulative' label so the visual encoding matches the caption's disclaimer.

issue: Vertical spacing is uniform despite unequal year gaps, so the diagram does not encode time proportionally and may imply equal intervals.
evidence: Labels are ~2017, ~2020, ~2022, ~2023, ~2024, ~2024, ~2025, ~2025, ~2026, but the bars are evenly spaced vertically.
acceptance_test: Either make vertical spacing proportional to the year markers or add 'not to scale' in the figure or caption so readers do not infer equal time intervals.

issue: The legend says 'Fleet (thick)' but the Agent Fleet bar's thickness is not visibly distinct from the other bars at print size, so the encoding is not reliably readable.
evidence: Legend reads 'Fleet (thick) — multi-model intelligence placement'. The Agent Fleet bar appears to have the same border/height treatment as the other bars; the 'thick' distinction is not obvious.
acceptance_test: Make the Fleet bar visibly thicker or remove 'thick' from the legend and use a clearer visual encoding for the fleet category.

issue: Visual-grammar mismatch: the figure is drawn as a vertical stack of equal-width bars with a single point-year per row, which reads as a layered substrate / causal sequence. The caption must explicitly rescue the reader from that false inference ('not a causal lineage and not a substrate stack: a later stage does not require the one before it, and the eras overlap'). Compounding this, the caption's claims that dates are 'approximate era markers' and that 'the eras overlap' are not visually encoded at all: each row shows one point year, not a span, so no overlap is depicted. The layout therefore both invites a wrong reading and fails to show the property the caption emphasizes.
evidence: Rendered page 461: nine full-width bars stacked with no gaps (Transformer ~2017 ... Agent Fleet ~2026), each with a single year label on the right and no horizontal duration. Caption: 'the ascending order is a chronology of selected milestones, not a causal lineage and not a substrate stack: a later stage does not require the one before it, and the eras overlap.' The authors' own 'not a substrate stack' warning confirms the geometry induces that misreading.
acceptance_test: Redesign so the geometry cannot be read as a stack/lineage and so era spans (and overlaps) are visible: use a horizontal time axis with each milestone drawn as a bar spanning its approximate era (start-end), rows ordered by time rather than by layer. After the change, a reader must not be able to infer 'Agent System requires Agent requires Tool-Using Model' from the layout, and at least one visible overlap between eras must appear.
